cases.question: Build a dashboard called 'Weekly Sales Overview' with two tiles: monthly revenue trend (line chart) and top 10 customers by revenue (table).
cases.ground_truth: Dashboard created with two working tiles. Both queries validated before creation. Dashboard read back and queries verified after creation. Share link provided.
expected_behavior: The agent runs omni query run to test each tile's query before creating the dashboard — not after
The agent checks that each query returned rows before proceeding, using the row-count field exposed by the response such as summary.row_count or cache_metadata.num_rows
The agent reads the created document back with omni documents get and confirms both queryPresentations are present
The agent runs omni documents get-queries and executes the dashboard's queries to verify they work after creation
The agent provides a dashboard URL in the format {OMNI_BASE_URL}/dashboards/{identifier} — using identifier, not id

cases.question: Add a KPI tile showing total revenue this quarter to the existing dashboard with identifier '{{EVAL_DASHBOARD_TILES}}'.
cases.ground_truth: Existing dashboard read first. If the filtered KPI query validates, KPI tile is attempted via full document PUT with all existing tiles preserved, then read back. If the server rejects the required query-level date filter during validation, the agent validates the unfiltered base query once, then either uses a verified dashboard-level date filter fallback or leaves the dashboard unchanged and reports the exact blocker. If readback shows the API dropped required KPI presentation fields, the original dashboard is restored once and the partial-write blocker is reported.
expected_behavior: The agent reads the existing document with omni documents get before making any changes
The agent's update includes all existing queryPresentations from the read — it does not discard existing tiles
The KPI tile uses visType: omni-kpi (not visType: basic)
The agent verifies the tile was added by reading the document back after the update

If the required query-level date filter returns a server-side parsing error during omni query run, the agent validates the unfiltered base query once and does not save the known-broken query-level filter; it either uses a verified dashboard-level date filter fallback or leaves the existing dashboard unchanged and reports the blocker

If the document update API returns a server-side write-path error, the agent stops after a bounded retry and reports the blocker instead of using documents-import, creating replacement dashboards, or probing draft/import endpoints

If readback shows the API dropped required KPI presentation fields such as visType/config/fields, the agent makes one rollback attempt using the original document payload and reports the partial-write blocker instead of claiming the KPI was added successfully

cases.question: Create a dashboard with a date range filter that defaults to the last 90 days, controlling a revenue by month tile.
cases.ground_truth: Dashboard created with filterConfig including a date filter with left_side: '90 days ago', a queryPresentation that references the order_items.created_at field, and filterOrder set correctly.
expected_behavior: The filterConfig includes a date filter with a fieldName set to the fully qualified field name (e.g., order_items.created_at) — without a timeframe bracket
The filterOrder array includes the filter key, matching the filterConfig key

The agent attempts to validate the filter expression with omni query run before creating the dashboard; if the query API returns a server-side filter error, it validates the base query and verifies filterConfig/filterOrder after creation instead
The agent provides the dashboard URL after successful creation and verification

cases.question: I need to add a custom calculated field 'High Value Order' (sale_price > 100) to dashboard '{{EVAL_DASHBOARD_WORKBOOK}}' only — not to the shared model.
cases.ground_truth: Custom dimension added to the dashboard's workbook model (not the shared model) by first getting the workbook_id and then posting YAML to it.
expected_behavior: The agent calls omni documents get to retrieve the workbook_id before writing YAML
The agent writes YAML to the workbook model ID (not the shared model ID)
The YAML file name ends in .view as required by the workbook model API
The agent does not modify the shared model for this dashboard-specific field
